summary: The scope fits B13 and there is no duplicate, overlap or design gap. But AC4 and AC7 would already pass on main. The rule that bots keep the throttle on while boosting also risks breaking existing append-only Dust Bowl bot tests (zero reversals, never stuck, lap bounds, finishing order) that the draft never mentions. A rewrite with non-vacuous criteria and a corner-safe boost rule should be approvable.

findings.claim: AC4 would pass on main as written. On main no AI ever arms, so 'a box taken by any car (including an AI) stays absent 300 ticks' only ever checks the player's own boxes. The test would not fail on main, as nightly tests must. AC4 also doesn't directly test the done_when clause 'a box an AI took is unavailable to the player until it respawns'.
findings.suggestedFix: Make AC4 non-vacuous: in a six-car Dust Bowl race, at least one box is taken by an AI car (index ≥1). That box stays absent for exactly 300 ticks. Add a direct player check: car 0 is unarmed and its input steers it through the spot of a box an AI took less than 300 ticks ago. Car 0 stays unarmed and the box stays absent (`RaceView.pickups[i]` false).

findings.claim: AC7 ('all six finish within 16200 ticks, and every AI car fired at least once or never got armed') passes on main: bots finish, and no AI is ever armed there. It proves nothing new tonight.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clause that fails on main, e.g. 'and at least one AI car fired a boost (its racer view showed boostTicks 90)'. Or require that every AI car armed before its last lap fired before finishing, with at least one such car.

findings.claim: 'While boosting they keep the throttle on' ignores Dust Bowl's tight corners. A bot carried at 32 into the tyre-lined turns may have to reverse, which breaks append-only tests the draft never mentions: dust-bowl-tight.test.ts:88-97 (2/4-car races, seeds 1–20, 0 reversals, never stuck); bot.test.ts:24-44 (lap bounds); positions.test.ts (seed 7 ends [2,1]); pickups.test.ts AC2 (car 0 armed within 600 ticks with 2 cars); pickup-replay.test.ts; pause-action-latch.test.ts.
findings.suggestedFix: Spec the boost rule as corner-safe. Fire only when armed, on dirt, on the ground, with no ramp approach or tight turn within ~48 units (90 ticks at 32) plus braking distance from 32 to the next corner's target. While boosting, hold throttle above the normal target only while no corner or ramp approach is within braking distance; otherwise brake to the target as today. Name the tests above as must-still-pass constraints.

findings.claim: Existing tests call stepCars(cars, inputs, track) with three arguments (push-out.test.ts, car-contact.test.ts, tests/sim/helpers.ts). If car.ts changes to boost several cars at once, the three-argument call must still mean 'no car boosted'.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep stepCars's extra parameter optional with today's default meaning none, e.g. an optional per-car boolean array.

findings.claim: Docs that would go stale and must be updated (not deleted): src/sim/types.ts:130 ('always false for AI cars'), the src/sim/pickups.ts header ('Only the player (car 0) collects and fires') and the stepWorld doc in world.ts ('Only car 0's action is read'). No module is retired, so supersedes is correctly empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask the builder to rewrite those three comments to describe per-car pickup state.

findings.claim: The harness lint flags createBot in AC1/AC2. createBot is the public sim export (src/sim/index.ts), the backlog item names it, and many existing tests use it, so naming it doesn't freeze an internal name.
findings.suggestedFix: No change needed; the rewrite may keep createBot(world, 0) as the car-0 driver.
